state.scope: Can is gaining the user-selected grouping of error branches and forwarding lines plus assertion/when labels. There are no outside consumers to protect. Decide how grouped error bodies may access payloads within this change; error-union redesign and live testing are outside the assignment.
state.facts: Current error arms are exhaustively checked exact nominal heads. An individual arm introduces the error name as its payload alias, or takes an explicit as name. Members of a group may have different payload shapes. A bare relay must keep its original completion and occurrence as well as data. The single source handler also owns a single set of nested invocation/fixture sites. One implementation compiles that body once and references the checked result from existing exact-type dispatch arms, requiring no additional runtime helper. All supplied grouping examples ignore payloads and return constants or invoke response constructors; inspecting a particular payload remains possible in a separate arm.
state.constraints: Do not weaken missing/duplicate-arm checks, specialization rules or the final ok convention. Standard [_] and success stay separate, and wrapper policy heads are unchanged. No inferred union or accidental reuse of an error-specific name should appear. Preserve grouped AST source formatting and expand shared test labels into independent roots/fixture selectors with existing execution settings, links and ordered queues.

payload_binding.instructions: Which rule for payload names should accompany the first version of grouped completion arms?

criteria.unbound_groups: Make grouped bodies unbound, reserving payload aliases for separate single-error branches.
criteria.explicit_union_alias: Support one shared union-typed alias and demand refinement before reading member payloads.
criteria.per_member_check: Admit payload usage by checking every alternative context, then reconcile the single lexical-site contract.
criteria.defer: Ship only relay and row-label grouping now, studying shared-handler payload semantics further.
